landed_against.rule: R-17/R-32/D-97 — no baseline moves inside this commit

qualifying_population.rule: C4 moves Abyssal Mask's Unmake off the kind ladder's DEBUFF_ARM (legacy phase 1.0, after the damage at its own timestamp) onto the new AURA_ARM rank (legacy phase -0.5, before it), because a persistent aura is already in force when the fight opens.  The packet's time is 0.0 and its ordering relative to every other timestamp is unchanged, so the only boundary that moves is t = 0.0 into a subject Unmake curses.  A leaf may therefore move only where it is (a) a leaf of a damage event at exactly t = 0.0 whose target is a participant the holder does not share a side with — including the support_damage_multiplier receipt container such an event gains when the aura prices it, whose spelling is read off the committed baseline's own amped events — (b) a leaf of an aggregate over (a): the breakdown row of every champion attacking or receiving one of those events, those participants' survival blocks, and the scenario's roster-wide objective / timeline_coverage / target_allocation blocks and duration, or (c) one of the snapshot's four shape counters, which move whenever a receipt subtree appears.  Enumerated from the committed scripts/golden_coupled_baseline.json and its participants[].items, before this slice's first src/ edit.

excluded_by_construction.fights/**: the pair engine's single-pair path.  golden_snapshot.py enters through pipeline.run_fight — one pair, no roster — so no snapshot row is ever priced by a cross-participant packet, and C4 changes no pair-side pricer: Abyssal's magic_amp term is untouched.  Structurally empty, not assumed empty.
excluded_by_construction.combat/support_events/**: the published support list is ordered by participant_timeline._published_support_phase, which classifies on kind alone and deliberately ignores a packet's declared rank, and the published payload is an explicit key list that carries no rank field.  Declaring AURA_ARM therefore moves no support-event leaf.

qualifying_population.cursed_derivation: item_support_effects._same_side folds team 'ally' onto 'main', so the ally is a teammate and the enemy is the only cursed participant.  Read off the committed baseline's participants[], not typed.
qualifying_population.empty_population_argument: No participant in any of the other twelve scenarios holds Abyssal Mask, and Unmake's packet is the only packet in src/ that declares AURA_ARM: every other damage_modifier keeps the kind ladder's DEBUFF_ARM.  Adding a member to TransitionRank renumbers the ordinals of DAMAGE and everything after it, but nothing sorts on the ordinal — every sort key consumes legacy_phase, whose floats are unchanged — so the renumbering is inert.  A leaf moving in any of the twelve is an unexpected occurrence and stops the slice (R-20).

c2_c4_overlap.rule: R-30: C2 and C4 partially cancel and both declare the holder's t = 0.0 magic leaves, so this set is enumerated in BOTH allowlists in advance and its presence in two is not an error.  These are events[0] — main's E into the cursed enemy at t = 0.0 — which C2 declared in dotted spelling and C4 declares in compare's own slash spelling; the twelve baseline leaves are the same twelve leaves.  C4's list carries a thirteenth path, the support_damage_multiplier receipt container clause (a) adds to every qualifying event, which C2's enumeration did not reach for this event.
c2_c4_overlap.measured_outcome: The overlap moved in neither slice, which a declared population permits and a lower bound would not: C2 gave Unmake an owner, so the walk skips the holder's own damage entirely, and arming the aura earlier cannot re-price a packet the owner skip removes.  Zero is a legal occurrence count (R-20) and the population is what makes that statement checkable.

qualifying_population.golden_population_argument: Structurally empty, not assumed empty: golden_snapshot.py enters through pipeline.run_fight — one pair, no roster — so no snapshot row is ever priced by a cross-participant packet, and C4 changes no pair-side pricer.  The published phase list and CAPABILITY_SCHEMA_VERSION reach no golden section: the committed pair baseline holds no capability payload.
qualifying_population.population_correction: The first enumeration run listed only the leaves the committed baseline already holds under a qualifying event, so it omitted the support_damage_multiplier container an event gains when the aura prices it.  The rule above is unchanged and that path is clause (a) under it; the script was corrected to read the receipt key's spelling off the baseline's own amped events and re-run against the same committed baseline, still measuring the pre-change tree.  Disclosed rather than silently widened — it is C2's disclosure in the other direction, an appearing receipt rather than a vanishing one.

carried_from_c2_and_c3.rule: R-17: C2, C3 and C4 all land against one frozen baseline, so the compare at this tip shows their moves too.  Re-measured at HEAD before this slice's first src/ edit and carried, not re-declared.

measured.coupled_golden: 55 differing leaves against the committed baseline: C2's and C3's 51 carried, of which 11 move further, plus 4 new — 15 leaves are this slice's own occurrences, measured as the C3 tip against this tip.  Every one lies inside the enumerated population; zero occurrences outside it.  11 of the 15 qualify for investigation under R-15 and each is owed an oracle receipt before the phase-boundary re-capture (R-19).  R-15's ratio clause is not triggered: the differing-leaf count is 0.18% of the numeric leaves, read from the report's own denominator.
measured.one_physical_cause: ally:Pantheon's R at t = 0.0 is the roster's only non-holder magic damage into the cursed enemy at the aura's own timestamp, and it gains the 12% it never had: 419.2 -> 469.5 = 419.2 * 1.12.  Everything else is an aggregate over that one packet, plus the Unmake receipt the event now carries.  The other three t = 0.0 events do not move and are in the population: main's E is the holder's own and the owner skip removes it (C2), and Pantheon's W and E are physical, which Unmake's declared damage_classes exclude (C3).

expected_diff_paths.coupled_exact_note: ``old`` is the value the committed exact baseline still holds — C2's and C3's moves have not been captured either — and ``new`` is this tip's.  C4's entries supersede C3's for the two keys they share, which is the later slice's declaration being the reachable one while three corrections land against one frozen baseline; C3's combat/0:main/outgoing entry is untouched because C4 does not move it.
